title: Sprain, strain, or possible dislocation
summary: Protect the joint, apply wrapped cold, and do not attempt to reduce a deformity.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Sprains and Strains
WHO Basic Emergency Care: Approach to the Acutely Ill and Injured
actions: Stop activity and support the injured joint in the position found.
Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth for up to 20 minutes at a time. A light compression wrap may help an ankle injury if it does not increase pain or impair circulation.
Elevate the limb when comfortable and when fracture or major injury is not suspected.
For obvious deformity, inability to use the joint, numbness, a cold or blue limb, or severe pain, keep it still and obtain urgent medical care.
Check colour, warmth, and feeling beyond any wrap; loosen it if these worsen.
prohibitions: Do not try to put a dislocated joint back in place.
Do not force movement to test the joint.
Do not wrap tightly enough to cause numbness, colour change, or more pain.

emergencyCall.text: Call emergency services for severe deformity, loss of feeling or circulation, or a high-energy injury.
